identified_issues: Safety controller claim of mechanical seal breach violates Rule of Direct Grounding by ignoring orthogonal sensor data.
Premature test abort proposal based solely on single-sensor pressure transient without multi-sensor correlation.
Misclassification of nominal cryogenic thermal duct contraction as dynamic face seal failure.
evidence: PT-401 recorded transient pressure drop of -1.15 bar over 140 ms before stabilizing at nominal base pressure of 38.2 bar, matching the expected -1.0 to -1.3 bar profile of thermal bellows contraction.
ACC-102 registered dominant acoustic peak at 44.2 Hz, which aligns directly with the duct resonant frequency range (40-48 Hz).

HE-SNIFF-01 recorded secondary purge helium concentration of 0.02 ppm at 14:22:10.600Z, remaining well below the seal breach threshold of >= 2.50 ppm and within ambient background (<= 0.05 ppm), conclusively disproving carbon face seal fracture.
recommended_action: Reject flight safety controller proposal to mark turbopump integrity as FAIL; proceed with chilldown sequence while updating automated abort criteria to require helium sniffer exceedance (>= 2.50 ppm) before triggering mechanical seal fracture interlocks.
